qt: to the Commission Per Clausen (The Left) Subject:

Data centres – and protests against them – are understandably becoming an increasingly hot topic in EU countries. The focus is partly on whether they are needed at all, given the scale at which they are currently being planned, and partly on who actually controls them. At the same time, their energy and water consumption is already a matter of concern. With a major increase in consumption on the horizon, this might not only have a negative impact on the EU’s climate efforts, but also lead to higher prices for both ordinary consumers and other businesses in the EU. There is therefore a need for clarity on how much this is expected to represent, so that we can have a proper discussion on what the real price of data centres will be. With the above in mind, can the Commission: 1.
Provide the estimated total energy consumption of existing data centres in the EU, and state how this is expected to increase over the next five years?
State how much water existing data centres in the EU are estimated to consume, and by how much that consumption is expected to increase over the next five years?
Provide an overview of how many data centres in EU countries – whether already completed or under construction – are wholly or partly owned by firms based outside the EU?
